hypothesis: The baseline product-form cut already gives the lowest crit_cross of all evaluated candidates; the parent's additive critical-pair star penalty fights it and inflates crit_cross, so instead I keep the cut/balance/binarisation backbone byte-identical and replace the additive penalty with a *mild multiplicative* reweighting of the cut term by a net-level criticality factor (1 + alpha*mean_crit_of_pins, alpha small, clamped), which can only nudge the cut toward keeping timing-critical nets intact without adding a competing gradient; this should lower crit_cross and crit-weighted cut (both strongly negative rho) and hence TNS.
analysis:
(1) Partially: crit_cross fell on C1 (0.011→0.005) and C3 (0.069→0.058) with lower wcut, but C3 dWNS collapsed (-51.9%) and total/robust are negative, so the mild reweighting did not translate to TNS gains.

(2) C1 improved broadly (cut 137→110, repair_flips 103→47); C3 cut/wcut barely moved yet crit_cross dropped—suggesting the factor nudged critical nets without reducing total crossings, and repair flips rose (353→361), plausibly destabilizing timing.

(3) seed_std=0.131 with C3 per-seed [-0.07,-0.46,+0.03] is too wide; not acceptable.

(4) Sweep alpha downward and add a repair-flip guard, validating on C3 seeds.
